translations.text: [?] dwells in them. They filled books for themselves with abominable words, so that the Lord will wipe them out along with their other plans, as it is written: “The plans of the ungodly will perish.”
Through the righteousness of all the righteous, they were called friends of God, like Abraham, the friend of God, and like the apostles whom the Lord called “my friends.”
But through the lawlessness of the heretics, Satan made them his friends, along with their other philosophers who grow their hair long like women.

The Lord Jesus, for his part, desires, according to what is written, that those who believe in him and love him, who keep his words, should be with him in his kingdom, so that they may see him in his glory and rest there forever.
Satan, for his part, eagerly pursues his desire to see all the heretics with him in the fiery furnace prepared for him
and his angels, as it is written, so that the heretics over whom he boasts, saying, “They are mine,” will see that his disgrace is theirs forever in Hades.
In faith, according to what is written, Abraham did not spare his beloved son because of his love for God, but offered him up when he was being tested.
The pagans, for their part, pour out the blood of their sons and daughters to demons, as it is written in the Psalms.
Unbelieving and ungodly kings have come from your offspring from the beginning, like Gog and Og and those like them, and King Herod, whom the Lord regarded as a fox—just like you yourselves.
Faithful kings, righteous kings, have come from the offspring of the Christians from the beginning down to the present.
The setting up of your gods from the beginning brought destruction upon your souls, and the bringing out of your idols in these present times has made you miserable, because those you set up
for yourselves as gods were smashed or shattered when the Christians dragged them facedown onto the ground, laughing and mocking your foolishness, raising their voices and letting out cries

like those who sing to a lyre, as their hearts rejoiced within them over the destruction of those whom people worship. They spoke [?] in this way: “[?] to you [?]. Bel has fallen; Dagon [?] is broken [?].”
“They are fashioned by hands. If wild animals and livestock carry them, they are bound like a load [?].”

And again: “The idols of the pagans are silver and gold, the work of human hands. Those who make them will become like them, along with everyone who trusts in them.” And again: “All the gods of the pagans are demonic idols.”
They say these things and many others as they sing praises to the blessed God, rejoicing over the comfort of their mother, the holy church, seeing her filled with crowds of people who believe in God

and his Christ, Jesus. They bow down and worship the Lord, as it is written: “Come, let us worship and bow down before him, and let us weep before the Lord who made us, because he is our God, and we are his people.”
They also laugh at your temples that have become deserted, and at all your other places where you offer sacrifices to what is worthless.
The journey of our God, Jesus Christ, brought devastation to your temples and established the catholic church.
It brought scattering to you, but it brought [?] the gathering together of his holy people.
Likewise, the cross of Jesus, the God of the Christians, became eternal life for them, and brought destruction to those whom you serve.
The Christians, the children of the King, Christ, the Lord Jesus, are in the light of life, as it is written. But the heretics, for their part, and all the ungodly pagans are in the [?]
[?], like a man who has [?] into a dark place. A covering [?] has been placed over him, so that those looking for him cannot see him.

This is how it is with the leaders of the pagans who have been unbelieving from the beginning. They have withdrawn into the place of darkness, which is Satan, and have gone astray through his deceits, his tricks, and his inventions.

And the covering of every kind of lawlessness has spread over them, as he reveals himself among them and fills them with darkness, like houses built beneath the ground without even a small opening for light.
Because God has abandoned them.
But like a man who has fled from a dark, deserted place into a place of light, with many cities surrounding him,

All the more, this is the condition of our ancient fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and those who came before them and those who came after them: they all fled from the deception in the world into the knowledge of the truth.
They came under the shadow of the Lord, the God of heaven, and, according to what is written, just as the light shines in the darkness and the darkness did not overcome it.
so it is with all their descendants, from the beginning until now: they shine through their good deeds, and the darkness of the entire race of heretics has not been able to overcome them.

You are the ones whom the written word addresses, O heretics: “You have crushed the teeth of sinners,” and, “Your tongue and your heart are empty. You have fallen through your own schemes, because of your many acts of impiety.”

The Lord has wiped you out because you angered him. Your memory has visibly perished. You have been defiled by the destruction you caused. You have grown old, and you foreign children of demons have limped away from your paths.
The Lord will tear you down and will not build you up.

The words of your mouths are lawlessness and deceit. You did not want to know what is good and do it. You thought about lawlessness on your beds; you took your stand on every evil path, and you did not hate wickedness.
Your hearts have gathered lawlessness for you. You have fallen before the face of God and his Christ, Jesus.
Coals have fallen upon you from his hand. He has cast you into a fire, because you are a senseless people who have insulted his name.
Your arrogance has continually risen up to him.
You have lifted your mouths up to heaven and spoken against God with violence. For this reason, [?] struck you as enemies and handed you over to everlasting disgrace.

A wind, which is the Lord’s anger, has blown upon you, and you have dried up. A storm, which is his wrath, will carry you away like stubble. For in just a little while you will cease to exist altogether.
For you are ignorant: you have been utterly put to shame, and you have dwindled little by little, together with all your descendants.
How have you come to decay like a rotten tree, O sinners who rejoice in what is empty? Or how have you dwindled, you enemies of the Lord?
Is it not because the Spirit of the Lord in the prophets speaks against you, saying, “Look, your enemies will perish, and everyone who practices lawlessness will be scattered”?
And again: “Sinners will perish from the earth,” or, “The lawless will be wiped out. The good will dwell on the earth, and the holy will remain upon it.” The lawless person
will be exposed—how greatly [?]! For it is a good scourge if we do not repent after hearing all these words that testify against us, together with those of the Scriptures.
Among the lilies that grow in the field and other very small things.
Wool is transformed into many forms, one color after another, by those who work with it.
But the ungodly person persists in his wickedness, as it is written. He has not been changed by all the words of God toward love, truth, and everything good.
God spoke many times and in many ways with his holy ones, instructing them about all his wishes. But he commanded Noah only once to build the ark.
And he completed his work and escaped the wrath that came down upon the earth—he and his entire household, together with various birds, various wild animals, and many domestic animals.
But we who do evil have not listened, even after all these words from God, to practice righteousness through which we will be saved.
God told Abraham only once to offer up his beloved son, and he acted quickly according to the Lord’s will, because he loved him more than his son.
But to this day we have not obeyed him in all his words, to present our bodies to him as a sacrifice in complete purity and complete truthfulness.
Nor did the angels speak at length with Lot to make him flee from those cities that the Lord burned with fire from heaven, from God.
But he quickly did what they commanded him.
But we have not obeyed God in all his words, to flee from every evil into every good and true deed.
Again, God spoke only one word to his disciples: “Follow me, and I will make you fishers of people.” They quickly left their nets, their boats, their father, and the hired workers, and followed him.
And this is how they received these great honors and this great glory from him through marvelous deeds.
But we have not obeyed him in all his words, to leave behind our desires and all our sins so that we might be worthy of his mercy and his blessing.
“To whom shall I testify so that he will listen?” For the holy and righteous, from our ancient fathers and the prophets down to our fathers the apostles, did not disobey God in carrying out
all his wishes. Rather, they also encouraged others, teaching them his ways, as it is written: “I will teach the lawless your ways, and the ungodly will turn back to you.”

Nor have we understood that we should do his will of our own free choice, as children who will inherit the kingdom of their Father in heaven. Nor have we obeyed his words and his teachings from the Scriptures, which compel us to submit.
